statement: Advanced Shadows shows shadow changes over a chosen solstice or equinox to check neighbor impacts.

source.ref: Analysis Hub: Advanced Shadows (solstice and equinox studies)

superiority: Accumulated hours of shadow maps with legend and export.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-desktop-20262 Acceptance sketch: Sun position and shadow polygons for 21 March at lat 40 equal reference to 0.1 degree and 1 cm.

statement: Annual illuminance evaluates yearly light levels using climate data (Labs).
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extending-sketchup/choosing-analysis-type Acceptance sketch: Compare to Radiance reference at sample points within 10 percent.

statement: Daylight factor simulates overcast sky ratio of interior to exterior illuminance.
superiority: Overcast-sky daylight factor runs on the GPU and the result grid can be compared against a Radiance run directly in the viewer.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extending-sketchup/choosing-analysis-type Acceptance sketch: CIE overcast sky closed form for a room; DF within 5 percent of the reference at 25 sensor points.

statement: sDA and ASE identify areas receiving too little or too much light.

source.ref: Analysis Hub: Underlit and Overlit (sDA and ASE)

superiority: Computes sDA and ASE from one shared annual simulation and shows the failing zones as editable regions.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Reference room with published sDA/ASE values; both metrics within 3 percentage points.

statement: Direct sun calculates duration of direct sunlight at points.
superiority: Direct-sun hours accumulate on any surface including curved ones, with an hourly breakdown on click.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Hours of direct sun on a 10x10 sensor grid compared with an independent ray-cast reference; max error 1 hour.

statement: Date and time view of daylight changes.
superiority: Time-series scrubber with synchronized sun path and result overlay for every analysis type.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Scrub hourly through one day; results at each hour equal the stored per-hour reference within 5 percent.

statement: Rules for preparing scenes (closed rooms, materials, sensor grids) for analysis.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Checklist validator flags defects on a fixture.

statement: Results viewer with false color, legends and dashboard that manages analyses.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extending-sketchup/using-analysis-dashboard Acceptance sketch: Legend scale and values match data.

statement: Flow to run analyses from a scene with sensor grids.
superiority: Runs locally or on a worker pool and reports progress, so long annual runs never block modeling.
notes: Acceptance sketch: End-to-end run on the reference scene produces a result file whose hash is stable across two runs.

statement: Analysis mode and the entity palette select surfaces for analysis.
superiority: Selection of analysis surfaces is by rule (tag, material, classification) rather than manual picking only.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extending-sketchup/entity-palette Acceptance sketch: Select 12 analysis surfaces by palette; the analysis report lists exactly those 12 surfaces.

statement: Sefaira web app evaluated building energy and daylight inside SketchUp.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extending-sketchup/getting-started-sefaira Acceptance sketch: Energy use index vs reference model.

source.ref: Revit and other BIM data in analysis

superiority: Imported metadata such as room names and areas feed analysis inputs and reports automatically.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Import a metadata-rich model; analysis report shows the imported room names and areas unchanged.

statement: Shadows toolbar sets date and time with sun direction from location.

source.ref: Sun and shadow study with Shadows panel and Date/Time

superiority: Documented, versioned solar-position algorithm with a stated error bound and a locked-in regression table.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Match to NOAA solar position algorithm within 0.1 degree for 50 sampled instants across the year at 3 latitudes.
